title: Unified Knowledgebase Migration Accelerator — engagement brief
body:
Summary:

This document captures a draft engagement plan and commercial sketch for a two-phase Knowledgebase Migration Accelerator offering. The target customer is a mid-size enterprise SaaS vendor (legal research scenario) that needs to migrate ~2.5M documents (mixed PDFs, HTML, and legacy txt) into a single searchable vector knowledgebase with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on Redwood Private/Dedicated.

High-level goals:
- Rapid onramp: demonstrate a working RAG flow with sample user queries within a 4-week POC.
- Production readiness: deliver a repeatable ingestion pipeline, vector store configuration, and a minimum viable serving topology for low-latency retrieval across 3 regions.
- Cost & SLO recommendations: provide recommended Dedicated instance profiles, quantization strategy, batching/cache settings, and a 6-month cost projection.

Engagement structure (two phases):

Phase A — Accelerated POC (4 weeks, fixed-scope)
- Week 0 (prep): onboarding, access provisioning, shared dataset sample definition (up to 50k docs).
- Week 1: ingestion proof (extraction + normalization), basic paragraphs/chunking heuristics, embedding prototype (batch).
- Week 2: vector store layout, retrieval tuning, eval harness (10 seed queries), latency baseline, first demo.
- Week 3: integrate Redwood hosted/de-dedicated model variant with streaming and fallback routing, auth + logging setup.
- Week 4: final demo, handoff checklist, runbook sketch, next-phase estimate.

Deliverables Phase A:
- Ingestion micro-pipeline (Python) + sample ETL scripts and docs.
- Embedding profile and vector schema (metadata fields, chunking rules).
- Demo app (notebook and small web UI) and evaluation report with precision/recall for seed queries.
- Runbook: deploy checklist, testing steps, and basic rollback plan.
- Phase B proposal with cost estimate and capacity plan.

Phase B — Production Onramp (12 weeks, time-and-materials with milestone caps)
- Ingest full corpus (up to agreed volume), reconcile data quality issues, complete connectors to source systems (SFTP, CMS API, internal DB).
- Hardened ingestion pipeline with monitoring, retry semantics, and backpressure handling.
- Deploy Dedicated serving cluster(s) with autoscale policies, per-region routing, and prefix/KV caching config.
- Integrate security controls: KMS for keys, VPC peering plan or on-prem connector, and audit logging.
- Deliver training for customer engineers and a 30-day hypercare window post-launch.

Phase B Deliverables:
- Production ingestion repo, CI, and infra-as-code templates (Terraform modules).
- Dedicated cluster sizing docs (GPU types, vCPU/memory, instance counts) and cost model.
- Observability dashboard templates: token-level cost, latency percentiles, error rates, and per-query trace links.
- SLA runbook, DR plan and maintenance schedule.

Assumptions (callouts)
- Customer provides representative sample data within 3 business days of kickoff.
- No heavy OCR cleanup required (if >5% of docs need advanced OCR + manual verification, additional effort estimate applies).
- PII classification is out of scope for Phase A; optional Phase B add-on.
- Network egress pricing and cross-region replication costs are excluded from Redwood fee estimates; customer cloud bills those directly.

Security & Compliance highlights
- Recommend Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS for PHI/PII projects.
- Data residency: we will deploy in customer region(s) only; any cross-region replication will be explicitly approved.
- Access: role-based access lists for ingestion service accounts and short-lived tokens for engineers.

Pricing sketch (high-level)
- Phase A fixed price: $45,000 (4 weeks, 3 engineers: solutions lead, data engineer, infra engineer). Includes up to 50k doc sample ingestion and two client-facing demos.
- Phase B time & materials: estimated $180k – $280k depending on connectors and OCR needs. Milestone caps and detailed T&M rates provided in formal SOW.
- Dedicated infra estimate (OPEX): baseline 2 x A100-equivalent pods for indexing/embedding offload + 3 x T4/RTX-class inference nodes for serving across regions. Approx. monthly infra run-rate: $14k–$30k (region dependent).
- Optional add-ons: extended 90-day monitoring + eval continuity ($12k), PII redaction pipeline ($25k), on-prem appliance install & validation ($40k).

Milestones & acceptance criteria
- POC kickoff complete: access provisioned and sample data verified. (Acceptance: access logs + sample ingestion success)
- Prototype demo: RAG demo answering 10/10 seed queries with accuracy threshold > 0.65 (acceptance: demo recording + eval report).
- Production readiness: end-to-end ingestion running in CI with canary deploy, retrieval latency p95 < 350ms for standard queries (acceptance: dashboard + smoke tests).

Operational considerations and recommended settings
- Chunking: 150–400 token target window by doc type, metadata preserved at chunk level to support filtering.
- Embeddings: use 1536-d profile for balanced accuracy/cost; provide quantized variant recommendation for Dedicated.
- Caching: prefix caching for repeated query patterns; recommend 12-hour TTL for embedding caches and 30-minute for retrieval result cache in front of model.
- Batching: tune batch sizes by median sequence length; we will propose continuous-batching knobs in the console templates.

Open questions for customer
- Expected peak qps and typical query size (tokens) per user session?
- Any regulatory constraints that mandate on-prem only deployment?
- Are there existing search/ranking heuristics to preserve (BM25 signals, domain taxonomies)?

Risks and mitigations
- Data quality: dirty/legacy formats can delay indexing. Mitigation: quick preflight QC scanner in Week 0 and scoped remediations.
- Cost variance: unpredictable query patterns can increase token spend. Mitigation: propose cost guardrails and per-route quotas during Phase B.
- Latency outliers: long-tail documents or large context queries could spike p99. Mitigation: tiered fallbacks to smaller model variants and early cutoff policies.

Workshop agenda (half-day, on-site or remote)
- 15m: introductions + success criteria alignment
- 30m: data walkthrough (sample doc types, sources, volumes)
- 45m: ingestion patterns + chunking decisions (interactive)
- 30m: architecture & serving topology: Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- 20m: cost model walkthrough and ops runbook preview
- 10m: open Q&A and immediate next steps

Next steps (recommended)
1) Approve Phase A fixed-price scope and sign 4-week SOW (target start: 2 weeks after approval).
2) Customer to share sample dataset + access matrix.
3) Schedule the half-day architecture workshop.
4) Solutions team to deliver kickoff deck and preflight QC script.

Notes to SEs (internal):
- Keep Phase A narrow: avoid full-text search parity goals — focus on RAG and retrieval accuracy for top-n answers.
- Capture anonymized eval results to add to Redwood public KB migration patterns playbook.
- Track time spent on OCR cleanup separately for transparent commercials.
